title: Can a small open model notice when it is being steered? Replicating steering-awareness

original_idea.body: Train a cheap probe to classify steered vs clean forward passes in an untuned small open model; report detection AUC vs steering magnitude.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain to evaluation-tooling assumptions about invisible steering, but the catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inject vectors + train logistic-regression probe on activations; very accessible, no fine-tuning.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single clean experiment: detection AUC vs steering strength/layer.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Probing-only, public models, no internal access; relevant to eval tooling and externally doable.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap probe training on a small model; single GPU or less.

novelty.reasoning: The untuned-probe-detects-steering question is flagged as unstudied vs the fine-tuned result.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Detecting steering via a simple probe on untuned models (vs fine-tuned detection) appears largely unstudied.
